types.name: Archetype
types.doc:
Entities sharing a component signature. Every entity with signature S lives
in exactly one Archetype keyed by S, and its columns are the only storage for
those components. AddComponent / RemoveComponent migrate the entity's data to
another archetype, which invalidates any component pointer held across it.

members.name: columnIndex
members.doc:
Dense ComponentID-indexed view of `columns` so the read hot path resolves
a column with one array index instead of a hashed lookup. Kept in sync by
PutColumn — columns are only ever added to an archetype, never removed.

members.name: entities
members.doc: Positions here correspond 1:1 with row indices into every column.

members.name: slots
members.doc:
The World slot of each row's entity, parallel to `entities`. A
swap-remove fixes the moved entity's row through it with an index, and
a ForEach hands it to Entity as a lookup hint — where a reverse
id → row hash map used to be.

members.name: ColumnData
members.doc:
Start of T's column, or null when this archetype does not carry T —
how a chunk pass reads an optional component without a per-entity lookup.

types.name: FEntityCommandBuffer
types.doc:
Structural changes recorded now and applied later, on the main thread, in
one go — the Mass command buffer. A worker or a ForEach that needs to add,
remove or destroy records here instead of submitting one std::function per
change (a heap allocation and an indirect call each): consecutive records of
the same kind and component type share one typed batch.

Playback runs the batches in recording order, with World::AddComponent /
RemoveComponent semantics per record — adding a component the entity
already carries leaves the existing value alone. A run of destroys goes
through World::DestroyEntities, which takes the lock once and orders the run
with SortForStructuralBatch, so the surviving layout depends on which
entities died, not on the order a worker happened to record them in.

A buffer is not thread-safe: one per recording thread.

members.signature: template<typename T> void AddComponent(EntityID entity, T value = T())

members.name: NumBatches
members.doc: Number of typed batches the records collapsed into.

members.name: Playback
members.doc:
Main thread, outside any ForEach — the same rule as the World calls it
makes. The buffer is empty afterwards and can be recorded into again.

members.name: SubmitTo
members.doc:
Queues the whole buffer on the World's deferred queue, which plays it
back at the end of World::Update. Safe from any thread, like
World::SubmitDeferred; this buffer is left empty.

types.name: FEntitySlotMap
types.doc:
EntityID → World slot: open addressing with linear probing over a
power-of-two table kept at most half full. std::unordered_map paid a node
allocation per entity and a pointer chase per lookup; an entity id is a
random 64-bit UUID, so here a lookup is almost always one probe into a flat
array. Erase shifts the rest of the probe run back instead of leaving a
tombstone, so a world that churns entities for hours never ends up probing
over dead buckets.

Concurrent Find calls are fine; every write is a World structural operation
and runs under the World's mutex.

members.doc:

The reference stays valid until the next FindOrAdd, Erase or Clear.

members.name: Clear
members.doc:

types.name: FModularSceneSystem
types.doc:
One world system contributed by a plugin (or a below-Game module).
Mirrors Scene's internal SceneSystemEntry: which registration set the
system belongs to (base = edit mode, simulation, runtime), where it
ticks outside World::Update (editorTick/simulationTick are explicit
sequence indices, -1 = skip), and what gets torn down on
Runtime/Simulation stop. The factory hooks are plain function pointers
so the descriptor stays trivially copyable across the DLL boundary.

ABI WARNING: plugins construct this struct with THEIR compiled layout and
the registry copies it with the engine's. Growing the struct therefore
requires rebuilding every plugin binary — a stale plugin registers a
short struct and the engine reads garbage past its end (a call through a
junk function pointer, first seen when OnSceneAttach was added). New
fields go at the END, every field must be null-tolerated, and
MOWO_MODULE_API_VERSION (Core/FModuleManager.h) must be bumped so the
loader refuses a plugin compiled against the old layout instead of
copying past its end.

members.name: void
members.doc:
Called after every ensure pass with the owning Scene — the modular
analogue of the SetSceneHooks/SetScene wiring blocks, so a plugin
system can spawn/destroy through the Scene's entity metadata instead
of raw World entities. Must be idempotent: Initialize, runtime start
and simulation start each re-run it. Scene is opaque down here — the
callback is only ever invoked from Scene itself.

members.name: RemoveAllInModule
members.signature: size_t RemoveAllInModule(void* moduleHandle, World* world = nullptr)
members.doc:
Drops every system whose hooks live inside the given module image —
the entries hold plain function pointers, so after the DLL frees they
are calls into unmapped pages. This also unblocks reload: the by-name
dedupe in RegisterSceneSystem would otherwise keep the STALE entry and
refuse the fresh module's registration. When `world` is non-null the
condemned systems' Remove hooks run against it first, so instances the
plugin allocated don't outlive the code their destructors live in.
Driven by the FModuleManager unload broadcast (with no world); the
hot-reload orchestrator calls it directly with the live world.
Returns the number of systems dropped.

members.name: SceneSystemRevision
members.doc:
Bumped whenever the system set changes so Scene can rebuild its cached
tick order instead of missing a module that loaded after the first tick.

types.name: SystemPhase
types.doc:
World::Update runs systems phase by phase in this order, preserving
registration order within a phase. Mirrors AActor::ETickGroup. The default
is PrePhysics, so systems that don't opt into a later phase keep their
relative order.

types.name: FSystemResources
types.doc:
World state that lives outside the component arrays. A system that
declares its component access declares these too, so two systems that both
reach the physics world (or a shared navmesh query) never share a batch;
before this, that rule lived only in a comment above BuoyancySystem.

members.name: DeclaresComponentAccess
members.doc:
Declaring reads and writes lets ComputeParallelBatches run this system
concurrently with non-conflicting systems in the same phase. Declaring
nothing means conflicting with everything, i.e. serial in registration
order — so this is purely opt-in.

members.name: GetDebugName
members.doc:
Names the profiler scope World::Update wraps around this system's
Update, so all registered systems show up in a capture without each
one carrying its own scope. The default resolves to the concrete type
(MSVC renders it "class Mowo::FCoverSystem"); the returned pointer
must outlive the frame, so overrides return string literals.

members.name: SystemsConflict
members.signature: static bool SystemsConflict(const System& a, const System& b)
members.doc:
Two systems conflict — must stay ordered and may not run together —
when either fails to declare its access, or their declared accesses
race: write/write on a shared component, or one's write touching the
other's read. Read/read alone never conflicts.

members.name: ComputeParallelBatches
members.signature: static std::vector<std::vector<size_t>> ComputeParallelBatches( const std::vector<System*>& systems)
members.doc:
Group systems (already filtered to one phase, in registration order)
into ordered batches. Every system within a batch is pairwise
conflict-free, so a batch can run concurrently; batches run in order.
A system never lands in an earlier batch than an earlier-registered
system it conflicts with, so dependent ordering is preserved. Levels:
level(i) = 1 + max level among earlier systems that conflict with i;
two systems at the same level are provably non-conflicting.

members.name: UpdateBefore
members.signature: void UpdateBefore(float deltaTime, const System* split)
members.doc:
One Update split at a system: UpdateBefore runs every system ahead of
`split` in update order and stops; UpdateFrom runs `split` and the rest
(and flushes the deferred queue, as Update does). The scene splits a
frame at PhysicsSystem when the step overlaps the DuringPhysics tick:
the systems ahead of it — input, movement intent, transforms — must
run before the step is kicked or they act a step late. A system the
world does not hold makes UpdateBefore run nothing and UpdateFrom run
everything.

members.signature: void UpdateFrom(float deltaTime, const System* split)

members.doc: Deserialization path — reuses a stored UUID

members.name: DestroyEntities
members.doc:
Destroys a set in SortForStructuralBatch order under one lock, with one
signature-version bump: the resulting layout is a function of the set,
whatever order it was gathered in. Unknown and dead ids are skipped.

members.name: SortForStructuralBatch
members.doc:
Reorders `ids` into the order a batch of structural changes to them
(destroy, add or remove a component) should run in: archetype creation
order, highest row first, then component-less ones in creation order.
Leaving an archetype swap-removes the row, so which survivor lands where
depends on the order the batch runs — and a set gathered from a hash
container arrives in hash order. Running it in this order makes the
resulting layout, and so every later ForEach, a function of the set
alone. Unknown or dead ids go last in their given order.

members.name: SetParallelSystems
members.doc:
When enabled, Update runs each phase's conflict-free system batches on
the job system. Only systems that declare component access are eligible;
an undeclared system conflicts with everything, so with none declared
every batch is one system and Update matches the serial phase loop.
Fan-out is also skipped when Update itself runs on a job worker.

members.signature: template<typename T, typename Func> void ForEach(Func&& func)

members.name: ForEachWith
members.signature: template<typename... Ts, typename Func> void ForEachWith(Func&& func)
members.doc:
Any number of required components; the lambda receives (Entity, Ts&...)
in declaration order. Widening a two-component pass to also fetch the
extra components it needs per entity beats per-entity GetComponent calls
inside the lambda.

members.name: ForEachChunk
members.signature: template<typename... Ts, typename Func> void ForEachChunk(Func&& func)
members.doc:
Archetype-at-a-time form of ForEachWith: the lambda receives
(Archetype&, Ts*...) — the start of each required column, rows
[0, arch.entities.size()). A pass that also wants an OPTIONAL component
reads it once per archetype through arch.ColumnData<T>() instead of a
hashed GetComponent per entity. Same thread and mutation rules as ForEach.

members.name: ParallelForEachWith
members.signature: template<typename... Ts, typename Func> void ParallelForEachWith(uint32_t rowsPerJob, Func&& func)
members.doc:
ForEachWith across the JobSystem: the rows of every matching archetype
cut into runs of `rowsPerJob` and spread over the pool, the calling
thread running its share (JobSystem::WaitForCounter helps). The lambda
gets (Entity, Ts&...) like ForEachWith and must write only the row it is
handed and read state nothing else writes meanwhile — the contract a
declared system in a parallel batch already keeps. Runs serially when the
pool is down, on a worker (a system already inside a parallel batch), or
when everything fits one job. Main-thread only, like ForEach.

members.name: GetLastParallelRunCount
members.doc:
Row runs the most recent ParallelForEachWith handed to the job pool; 0
when it ran serially. Diagnostics and tests only.

members.name: ForEachEntity
members.signature: template<typename Func> void ForEachEntity(Func&& func) const
members.doc:
Every living entity, unfiltered. Main-thread only. Order is defined:
archetype creation order then row order, then component-less entities
in creation order. It walks a snapshot, so the callback may add or
remove components; an entity it destroys is skipped, one it creates is
not visited.

members.name: MakeQuery
members.doc: Declared here so callers need no extra include; the body lives in Query.h.

members.name: IsIterating
members.doc:
True while a ForEach / ForEachWith pass is running on any thread. The
structural mutators MOWO_CHECK this is false: mutating from inside a
ForEach lambda swap-removes the very row the loop cached a raw column
pointer into, so the guard aborts loudly instead of corrupting it.

members.name: GetSignature
members.doc:
Empty bitset if the entity has no components yet (the row only exists
after the first AddComponent), which matches a no-requirements query.

members.name: GetSignatureVersion
members.doc: Bumped on every entity creation, destruction, AddComponent, RemoveComponent.

members.name: GetArchetypeVersion
members.doc:
Bumped ONLY when a new archetype is created; archetypes are never pruned
at runtime. A Query's cached (archetype, columns) buckets go stale only
when a new archetype appears, not when entities move between existing
ones (Each() reads live entity counts), so queries key their cache on
this instead of the per-mutation signature version.

members.name: ForEachMatchingArchetype
members.signature: template<typename Func> void ForEachMatchingArchetype(const std::bitset<MAX_COMPONENTS>& required, Func&& func) const
members.doc:
Every archetype whose signature is a superset of `required`, so a query
rebuild walks matching archetypes instead of every entity's signature.

members.name: SubmitDeferred
members.doc:
Threads that can't take the World mutex — because a ForEach is up the
stack, or to batch many small mutations — submit a callable instead.
Submit is thread-safe; the lambda runs on the main thread and may call
any World API. FlushDeferred runs at the end of World::Update, after
every system and outside any ForEach. Calling it manually elsewhere is
fine, but never re-enter it from inside a ForEach lambda.

free.name: GetMatchList
free.signature: inline const std::vector<Archetype*>& World::GetMatchList(const ComponentID* ids, size_t count)
free.doc:
The cache clear/build races only with itself (two iterations starting
concurrently after a structural change), never with a live consumer: the
version can only move via structural ops, which MOWO_CHECK !IsIterating(),
so an in-flight pass pins the version and no concurrent GetMatchList can
clear the entry it iterates. Mapped vectors are reference-stable across
inserts, so the returned reference survives other lists being cached.
